verdict.line: You lose if you stand in melee letting Tahm Kench land repeated hits until An Acquired Taste hits three stacks for a stun or Devour kill; you win if you dash in with E, burst, and leave before that third hit lands.

brief.thesis: Kled's E (Jousting) lets him pick exactly when a trade starts and ends, which denies Tahm Kench the repeated hits he needs to stack An Acquired Taste to three and threaten a Q stun or an outright R (Devour). That threat only materializes if Kled stays in prolonged melee range, which is precisely the mistake OP.GG flags for this matchup. A 52.8% win rate over 72 games with a clear solo-kill edge confirms this is Kled's lane to dictate, not Tahm's.

theirWindow.when: He's landed two hits on you
theirWindow.what: He's one hit from three stacks, meaning his next Q (Tongue Lash) stuns you or he can R (Devour) you outright for magic damage based on his total health. Disengage immediately instead of trading a third time.

yourWindow.when: Skaarl's HP is full, E ready
yourWindow.what: Dash in with E (Jousting), land Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) for the hook and yank bonus damage, pop W (Violent Tendencies) for the attack speed burst, then recast E to dash back out before he's landed enough hits to stack three.

powerCurve.note: Neither combo threatens an all-in yet.
Joust bursts outrun Tahm's single-target poke.
R adds burst before Devour stacks threaten.
Tahm's Q sustain starts evening out dueling.
Caught alone, stacked Devour burst kills fast.

start.why: The 81.1% pick rate reflects the matchup plan: short, decisive E trades need raw AD and sustain, not passive scaling, since you're looking to win exchanges before Tahm can stack his passive.

boots.why: Tahm's entire kit — Q, W, and R — deals magic damage, and the tenacity shortens the stun window if he lands a third stack of An Acquired Taste off Q.

core.why: Health and AD scaling keep Skaarl's HP bar high, which is exactly the resource you need full before committing to a Joust trade.
Armor shred and health help you push through Tahm's passive, which gives him extra damage based on his total health — he gets tankier and harder-hitting the longer a fight runs.
The health and shield proc cover you if Tahm lands his Devour combo, turning a potential kill into a survived trade.

situational.when: you're sieging or split-pushing away from Tahm's melee range
fights are running long and you need sustained damage against his health-scaled tankiness
you need more AoE and mobility for skirmishes beyond the 1v1

runes.keystoneWhy: The measured 58.3% win rate page builds around sustained duels — Conqueror's stacking adaptive force rewards exactly the extended Joust-in, auto, Joust-out pattern you need to win before Tahm stacks his passive.

summoners.why: Flash + Ignite is the standard pick (78% of games) and backs up your measured solo-kill advantage with real kill pressure during the level 3-5 window. Flash + Teleport is run less often but shows a notably higher 72.7% win rate in the sample — worth taking if you expect this to be a slower, split-push-oriented game rather than an early kill lane.

playing.title: Trade with E, not your face
playing.detail: OP.GG's own warning is specific: avoid prolonged melee combat with Tahm Kench. Dash in with E (Jousting), land your damage, and recast E to leave rather than standing in auto-attack range.

playing.title: Count his stacks before every trade
playing.detail: An Acquired Taste builds from any damage Tahm lands on you. At three stacks his Q (Tongue Lash) stuns instead of slows, and he becomes able to R (Devour) you for magic damage. Never trade through two stacks.

playing.title: Only commit with Skaarl topped up
playing.detail: Kled deals full damage to champions while mounted; once Skaarl's HP bar empties and you dismount, your Q becomes the weaker Pocket Pistol and your champion damage drops. Reset before forcing anything.

playing.title: Hunt the level 3-5 kill window
playing.detail: Jousting and Violent Tendencies both come online by level 3-5, giving you burst that outpaces Tahm's single-target Q poke on its 7-5s cooldown. This is where your measured solo-kill advantage comes from — use it.

playing.title: Bank R for a forced skirmish
playing.detail: Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is on a 140/125/110/110/110s cooldown, so don't throw it carelessly. Hold it to collapse a fight in your favor or to punish Tahm's Abyssal Dive (W) if he overcommits with it.

playing.title: Don't feed stacks while dismounted
playing.detail: When Skaarl is down, you hit champions for less and trade from a weaker position. Back off and farm with Pocket Pistol until courage remounts you instead of feeding Tahm free damage toward his passive.

playing.title: Keep the wave contested
playing.detail: Tahm Q heals him on champion hits and lets him shove safely if left unchecked. Stay on the wave so he can't push freely and set up a safe Abyssal Dive engage or freely stack sustain.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoner spell choices are pulled directly from measured Kled vs Tahm Kench games on the current patch (16.20.1); the stack-count tells, power-curve timing, and trade-pattern reasoning are my own read of how the two kits interact.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid fighting Tahm Kench in melee combat as he can easily get a kill. Do not let him push lane by focusing on contesting and farming lane.
